start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-jobs-handed-between-ais on my store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} to hand the job p-one from ai:east to ai:north."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the AI and job records are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-jobs-handed-between-ais" with store, and the tool row and its input (for example tool:hand-a-job-to-an-ai with as, job, to and key).
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts; every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.

4. Each run reads the AI and job records from the store, runs the tool over them, applies its keep list to the store in one transaction, and reports what was written, and any write refused because the job changed (read again, then decide again).

worked_examples.title: Hand a job from one AI to another and keep it
worked_examples.ask: Give ai:north the job "Water the plants" from ai:east, so it waits for ai:north to take.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The store holds ai:east and ai:north as ai records and no job p-one.
worked_examples.hands_back: Run answers written 1 and refused 0; the store now holds "ai-job:p-one" with status "waiting", sent by "ai:east" to "ai:north".
